evidence:
Built the criterion -> requirement map for all 47 functional, 5 polish, 5 visual and 2 gate criteria. Nearly every graded demand traces to hireops_rules.md or instruction.md: one-stage moves (rules s3 'Skipping a stage is refused'), bottom arrival / board-order bulk arrival (s3), reorder with ordinary controls (s3), 1-50 whole interview places (s2), case-insensitive duplicate email shown at field with typed text kept (s2), reject reason/rejected-from/reopen/reason cleared and restored by undo (s3), Interview capacity incl. bulk and undo (s3), focus on card controls after refused move (s3 'keyboard focus stays on that card's controls'), 409 naming who (s3), undo rules incl. reorder superseding (s3: 'moved up or down', managers 'move ... including re-ordering'), activity lines newest first with job filter (s4), 15 s live updates preserving typing/focus/open card/scroll (s5), Enter/Shift+Enter, empty focused box, failed send stays (s6), 30-message pages with remaining count and stable anchor (s6), per-person unread (seed check: Mei read_count 1 of 3 APP-201 messages, 2 later from Tomas -> 2 unread, matches hro_unread_counts), seen rules excluding observer (s6), drafts per person/conversation/browser surviving reload and sign-out, hidden from other users (s6, instruction l.7), candidate wording table and privacy list (s7), 401/403/404 (s1), restart persistence (instruction l.15). Sign-in usage and the render gate's wrong-password refusal are house convention per SKILL.md known false positives and workbook E28. No exact route, label, selector or layout is graded (prompts: 'Do not require routes, selectors, field names, layouts or exact wording').

DEFECT (reported per instance): several functional criteria make 'not offered' in the UI part of the pass statement although the public rules only require server refusal and expressly leave controls to the implementer (hireops_rules.md l.3-5: 'Routes, field names, element ids, button labels and the shape of the pages are yours'; l.52 'Dragging may be offered as well'; instruction l.3 'If a move is refused, put the card back where it really is and tell me why', which presumes refusable moves can be attempted from the UI). Instances:
(1) task/tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:56 hro_move_one_stage (w1.5): 'a move that skips a stage (Interview to Hired) is not offered and, when tried, is refused'.
(2) judge.toml:92 hro_reject_hired (w0.5): 'the option is not offered and, when tried, is refused'.
(3) judge.toml:155 hro_mgr_early_refused (w1): 'Applied to Screen and Screen to Interview ... are not offered and, when tried, refused'.
(4) judge.toml:164 hro_mgr_other_job (w1): 'is offered no move on this job's cards' (rules s3 only say such moves are refused; whether another job's manager even sees that board is unspecified).
(5) judge.toml:254 hro_undo_once (w1): 'no undo is offered for it again'; prompt.md:33 B(4) 'no undo is offered any more' and B(11) 'check that the V-and-X move is no longer offered for undo'. Rules s3 only say undo is refused.
The 'Fails if' clauses of (1)-(5) list only acceptance, so the conjunctive pass sentence and the fail sentence disagree; a judge reading the pass sentence literally can zero a conforming app. These conditions mirror the golden's own presentation choice: board.js:144-152 targets() lists only legal one-stage targets, board.js:367 hides Undo when nothing is undoable. Yet the golden itself 'offers' skips via drag (board.js:300-318 accepts a drop on any column and lets the server refuse), so under a strict reading even the golden's drag surface conflicts with (1). REVIEW_POLICY.md: 'A default chosen by the golden is not automatically a requirement.' Weight at risk on a conforming alternative: up to 5.0 of the functional weight total.

Borderline / Note-level (professional default, not counted as the defect): hro_observer_readonly judge.toml:173 'Fails if any is offered' and hro_thread_access judge.toml:362 'Observer reads it with no way to send' - hiding write controls from a read-only role is a defensible professional default, though rules s1/s3 only require refusal. hro_refused_put_back judge.toml:137 with prompt.md:29 requires the UI to let the user attempt a move into a full Interview; an app that pre-disables '-> Interview' when the column shows 2/2 is not barred by the rules (s3 'Shown at once, put back if refused') and could score 0 because the protocol's only put-back observation then cannot occur. hro_add_candidate judge.toml:38 'appears ... with the entered name and email' could be read as requiring the email on the card face; rules s3 only say a card can be opened to show its details. hro_pol_failed_send polish judge.toml 'A visible explanation appears' and 'nothing was added to the conversation' go slightly beyond rules s6 ('stays in the box'); an optimistic bubble marked 'not sent' is an ordinary pattern. hro_pol_live_board 'scroll the page so it is not at the top' presumes a scrollable page.

No configured judge run, Oracle or model score exists (raw-evidence-index scope: 'Full configured grading/workload, reward discrimination/ranking and Oracle/target scores are absent'), so whether a judge actually false-fails these is unmeasured; the scripted golden run cannot exercise an alternative UI.
counterexample: Conforming alternative: a board whose per-card 'Move to' select lists every stage (and supports dragging to any column, as the golden also does), shows a persistent 'Undo last move' button, and lets the server refuse illegal choices with a 403/409/422 and a visible reason, putting the card back. It satisfies every rule in hireops_rules.md s3 (skips, Hired rejections, manager early moves, other-job moves and repeated/superseded undos are all refused and change nothing). A judge following the pass sentences of hro_move_one_stage ('is not offered and, when tried, is refused'), hro_reject_hired, hro_mgr_early_refused, hro_mgr_other_job and hro_undo_once ('no undo is offered') records 'offered' and can assign 0 to up to 5.0 functional weight. Plausible broken app that still passes these rows: an app that hides the illegal options client-side but whose server accepts the replayed skip - correctly caught, since the 'when tried'/replay leg remains.
suggested_fix: In hro_move_one_stage, hro_reject_hired, hro_mgr_early_refused, hro_mgr_other_job and hro_undo_once (and prompt B(4)/B(11)), replace 'is not offered and, when tried, is refused' / 'no undo is offered' with 'is refused with the card unchanged whether tried through the UI or, if not offered, by replay; hiding it is optional', matching the existing 'not offered or is refused' wording of hro_reopen and hro_notes; optionally let hro_refused_put_back accept a UI that pre-blocks the full-Interview move with a visible reason and then observe put-back on a stale-board refusal.
